title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.17680v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Building a co-registered SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth Observation is above all an acquisition problem, yet the main multi-modal datasets are collected opportunistically, with no per-stratum quota control and no mechanism against the geographic dropout that non-uniform cloud cover leaves behind. We present Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition (DDSA), an algorithm that treats building a co-registered Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over a hemisphere-corrected (class x season x region) stratification, enforces strict temporal pairing and a multi-stage quality gate, and closes the loop during acquisition with a human-in-the-loop deficit-repair stage. Measured on its own product, the algorithm yields three results a single-pass acquisition cannot report. Deficit-driven ordering makes a partial run a covering one: it holds every one of the 192 strata populated from the first few

translated_title: 基于缺口驱动的分层采集方法构建 STRATA-S12：一个面向自监督学习的开放 SAR-光学数据集
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.17680v2 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：为自监督地球观测构建一个配准的 SAR-光学语料库，本质上首先是一个数据采集问题，然而目前主要的多模态数据集都是机会性采集的，既没有分层的配额控制，也没有应对非均匀云覆盖所导致的地理数据缺失的机制。我们提出了缺口驱动的分层采集（DDSA）算法，该算法将构建配准的 Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 语料库视为在经过半球校正的（类别×季节×区域）分层上的约束最大覆盖问题，执行严格的时间配对和多阶段质量把关，并在采集过程中通过人机协同的缺口修复阶段形成闭环。在该算法自身产品上的测量表明，该算法取得了单次采集无法报告的三项结果。缺口驱动的排序使得部分运行也能成为覆盖性运行：它使 192 个分层中的每一个从最初几个……
tldr: 提出了缺口驱动分层采集算法（DDSA），将构建配准的 Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 数据集建模为半球校正分层上的约束最大覆盖问题，并通过人机协同的缺口修复机制确保全部 192 个分层得到完整覆盖，为自监督地球观测学习提供了高质量的开放 SAR-光学语料库。
en_tdlr: Proposes Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition (DDSA), which frames building a co-registered Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over hemisphere-corrected stratification with human-in-the-loop deficit repair, ensuring full coverage of all 192 strata for an open SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth observation.
